# manual case: filesystem case-sensitivity of the directory holding the repro
# ran: 2026-08-07T00:59:10Z
# why: #8527 is only meaningful on a case-insensitive filesystem. Windows 10+
#      supports a PER-DIRECTORY case-sensitivity flag, so this must be measured,
#      not assumed, before any claim about what the repro demonstrates.
# shell: PowerShell

$ (Get-Location).Path
<triage>\data\issues\8527

$ fsutil file queryCaseSensitiveInfo .
Case sensitive attribute on directory <triage>\data\issues\8527 is disabled.

$ (Get-Volume -FilePath .).FileSystem
NTFS

$ [IO.Directory]::GetFiles('.', 'cs_*ragma.hlsli')   # the ONE real name on disk
cs_pragma.hlsli

$ [IO.File]::Exists('cs_Pragma.hlsli')   # capital P; resolves anyway -> case-insensitive
True

$ (New-Object IO.FileInfo (Join-Path (pwd) 'cs_Pragma.hlsli')).Length   # opens, same file, same size
56
$ (New-Object IO.FileInfo (Join-Path (pwd) 'cs_pragma.hlsli')).Length
56

# Conclusion: NTFS with per-directory case sensitivity DISABLED. Exactly one file
# named cs_pragma.hlsli exists; the spelling cs_Pragma.hlsli opens that same file.
# Everything below in out-*.txt / variant-*.txt is therefore a WINDOWS result. On a
# case-sensitive filesystem the same repro would fail with 'file not found' instead.
